allQuestions.questionText: What important decision did Zeus make to relieve the Earth from too many people?
allQuestions.answerA: To cause a great flood
allQuestions.answerB: To cause the Trojan War
allQuestions.answerC: To send monsters to the humans

allQuestions.questionText: On which mountain did the glorious wedding of Peleus and Thetis take place?
allQuestions.answerA: On Mount Pelion
allQuestions.answerB: On Mount Olympus
allQuestions.answerC: On Mount Parnassus

allQuestions.questionText: Which goddess was NOT invited to the wedding and why?
allQuestions.answerA: Athena, because she was busy
allQuestions.answerB: Aphrodite, because she didn't like weddings
allQuestions.answerC: Eris, the goddess of discord, because she caused fights

allQuestions.questionText: What did Eris throw among the guests out of her anger?
allQuestions.answerA: A magic potion
allQuestions.answerB: A golden apple that said 'To the fairest'
allQuestions.answerC: A poisoned arrow

allQuestions.questionText: Where did Zeus send Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite to settle their dispute?
allQuestions.answerA: To Mount Ida, so the shepherd Paris could choose
allQuestions.answerB: To the oracle of Delphi
allQuestions.answerC: To the sea, to ask Poseidon

allQuestions.questionText: Who was the shepherd Paris in reality?
allQuestions.answerA: A disguised god
allQuestions.answerB: The prince of Troy, son of Priam
allQuestions.answerC: The greatest warrior of Sparta

allQuestions.questionText: What did the goddess Athena promise Paris if he gave her the golden apple?
allQuestions.answerA: Boundless wealth and power
allQuestions.answerB: The most beautiful woman in the world
allQuestions.answerC: Wisdom and victories in wars

allQuestions.questionText: What did Paris do as soon as he chose Aphrodite and she told him about Helen of Troy?
allQuestions.answerA: He traveled to Sparta to take her
allQuestions.answerB: He stayed on the mountain guarding the sheep
allQuestions.answerC: He went to Mycenae to find Agamemnon

allQuestions.questionText: What did Menelaus decide to do when Paris stole Helen from him?
allQuestions.answerA: To forgive him and find another wife.
allQuestions.answerB: To ask the other kings for help to get her back.
allQuestions.answerC: To go to Troy alone in a small boat.

allQuestions.questionText: Who was appointed commander of all the Greek kings in the campaign against Troy?
allQuestions.answerA: Agamemnon, the king of Mycenae.
allQuestions.answerB: Odysseus, the king of Ithaca.
allQuestions.answerC: Menelaus, the king of Sparta.

allQuestions.questionText: Why couldn't the Greek ships depart from the port of Aulis?
allQuestions.answerA: Because they didn't have enough weapons and food.
allQuestions.answerB: Because there was a storm and huge waves.
allQuestions.answerC: Because there was no wind blowing, because Agamemnon had angered the goddess Artemis.

allQuestions.questionText: What was the only solution, according to the seer Calchas, for the wind to blow again?
allQuestions.answerA: For Agamemnon to sacrifice his daughter, Iphigenia.
allQuestions.answerB: To build a great temple for the goddess Artemis.
allQuestions.answerC: For everyone to return to their homes.

allQuestions.questionText: What did Agamemnon finally decide to do, despite feeling unbearable sorrow?
allQuestions.answerA: He canceled the war and returned to Mycenae.
allQuestions.answerB: He agreed to sacrifice Iphigenia for the good of Greece.
allQuestions.answerC: He asked his brother to take his place.

allQuestions.questionText: What happened at the last moment, right before Iphigenia's sacrifice took place?
allQuestions.answerA: The goddess Artemis snatched her away and put a deer in her place.
allQuestions.answerB: Achilles saved her and took her away.
allQuestions.answerC: Zeus threw lightning bolts and stopped the sacrifice.

allQuestions.questionText: Who did the Achaeans meet in Delos and what did he give them so they would have food during the war?
allQuestions.answerA: The god Apollo, who gave them golden bows.
allQuestions.answerB: The king of Delos, who gave them golden coins.
allQuestions.answerC: The seer Anius, who gave them his daughters, the Oenotropae (they made wine, oil, and wheat).

allQuestions.questionText: Who were the rulers of Troy when the ships of the Achaeans arrived there?
allQuestions.answerA: Priam and Hecuba
allQuestions.answerB: Menelaus and Helen
allQuestions.answerC: Agamemnon and Clytemnestra

allQuestions.questionText: Who was Cassandra, the daughter of the king of Troy?
allQuestions.answerA: A brave female warrior who defeated Achilles.
allQuestions.answerB: A seer who told the truth, but the gods made it so no one would believe her.
allQuestions.answerC: The most beautiful woman in Troy, whom Odysseus fell in love with.

allQuestions.questionText: Who was the bravest warrior and commander of the Trojan army?
allQuestions.answerA: Paris
allQuestions.answerB: Aeneas
allQuestions.answerC: Hector

allQuestions.questionText: Why did no Achaean dare to step on the land of Troy first?
allQuestions.answerA: Because an oracle said that the first to step on land would be killed.
allQuestions.answerB: Because the sand was too hot.
allQuestions.answerC: Because they were afraid of the high walls of Troy.

allQuestions.questionText: What cunning trick did Odysseus play to get out first, but without stepping on the dirt?
allQuestions.answerA: He wore winged shoes and flew over the shore.
allQuestions.answerB: He had someone else carry him on their back.
allQuestions.answerC: He threw his shield on the ground and stepped on it.

allQuestions.questionText: Which Olympian gods supported the Greeks (Achaeans) in the war?
allQuestions.answerA: Zeus and Pluto.
allQuestions.answerB: Hera, Athena, and Poseidon.
allQuestions.answerC: Ares, Apollo, and Aphrodite.

allQuestions.questionText: For how many years did the Achaeans fight around the walls of Troy without being able to conquer it?
allQuestions.answerA: 10 years
allQuestions.answerB: 1 year
allQuestions.answerC: 100 years

allQuestions.questionText: Which great Greek leaders argued fiercely in the tenth year of the war?
allQuestions.answerA: Odysseus and Menelaus.
allQuestions.answerB: Agamemnon and Achilles.
allQuestions.answerC: Paris and Hector.

allQuestions.questionText: Who was Chryses and why did he go to the Achaean camp?
allQuestions.answerA: He was a priest of Apollo and went to ask for his daughter back, offering a great ransom.
allQuestions.answerB: He was a Trojan spy who wanted to steal their weapons.
allQuestions.answerC: He was a friend of Achilles and brought him gifts from Greece.

allQuestions.questionText: How did the god Apollo punish the Achaeans because Agamemnon rudely turned away his priest?
allQuestions.answerA: He threw lightning bolts and burned their ships.
allQuestions.answerB: He raised huge waves and drowned many soldiers.
allQuestions.answerC: He shot invisible arrows and brought a terrible disease (plague) to the camp.

allQuestions.questionText: Who did the Achaeans ask to find out why they were getting sick and what did he tell them?
allQuestions.answerA: The seer Calchas, who explained that it was due to Apollo's anger.
allQuestions.answerB: The god Zeus, who told them to return to Greece.
allQuestions.answerC: King Priam, who apologized to them.

allQuestions.questionText: What was Agamemnon forced to do to stop the evil and the disease?
allQuestions.answerA: Sacrifice a golden deer to the god Apollo.
allQuestions.answerB: Return his daughter to the priest Chryses.
allQuestions.answerC: Defeat Hector in a duel.

allQuestions.questionText: When Agamemnon returned the priest's daughter, what did he forcefully take from Achilles, making him extremely angry?
allQuestions.answerA: His golden sword and his shield.
allQuestions.answerB: His beloved friend, Patroclus.
allQuestions.answerC: His beautiful slave, Briseis, causing Achilles to withdraw from the battle.

allQuestions.questionText: How did the war go for the Achaeans without Achilles and what did Agamemnon do?
allQuestions.answerA: They were winning easily and didn't need him at all.
allQuestions.answerB: They kept losing and Agamemnon sent him rich gifts to beg him to return.
allQuestions.answerC: They made new, stronger weapons and Agamemnon didn't care.

allQuestions.questionText: What terrible feat did Hector, the leader of the Trojans, manage to achieve while Achilles was absent?
allQuestions.answerA: He reached the Achaean ships and started burning them.
allQuestions.answerB: He stole Achilles' horses from inside his tent.
allQuestions.answerC: He surrendered to Odysseus to save himself.

allQuestions.questionText: What did Patroclus ask of his friend Achilles when he saw the great danger?
allQuestions.answerA: To give him his armor to wear and scare the Trojans, and Achilles agreed.
allQuestions.answerB: To leave secretly at night with the ships, but Achilles refused.
allQuestions.answerC: To go talk to Hector to make peace.

allQuestions.questionText: What finally happened to Patroclus in the battle, while wearing Achilles' armor?
allQuestions.answerA: He tripped and fell into the sea.
allQuestions.answerB: He fought bravely, but eventually Hector killed him.
allQuestions.answerC: He defeated all the Trojans by himself and became a hero.

allQuestions.questionText: What happened around the body of the dead Patroclus?
allQuestions.answerA: The Achaeans and Trojans immediately stopped the war to bury him.
allQuestions.answerB: A fierce battle broke out for his body and Hector took his armor.
allQuestions.answerC: The gods immediately took him up to Mount Olympus.

allQuestions.questionText: How did Achilles react when he found out that his best friend, Patroclus, was killed?
allQuestions.answerA: He wept bitterly and decided to return immediately to the battle to avenge him.
allQuestions.answerB: He was terrified and hid in his tent.
allQuestions.answerC: He forgave Hector and asked for the war to stop.

allQuestions.questionText: What did Achilles do the day after the death of his beloved friend, Patroclus?
allQuestions.answerA: He left angrily with his ships for Greece.
allQuestions.answerB: He put on his new armor, threw himself into battle, and killed many Trojans.
allQuestions.answerC: He stayed in his tent crying without doing anything.

allQuestions.questionText: What did the Trojans and Hector do when they saw the furious Achilles approaching the walls?
allQuestions.answerA: The Trojans hid terrified inside the city, but Hector stayed outside to face him.
allQuestions.answerB: They all went out of the walls together to fight Achilles.
allQuestions.answerC: Hector hid and the rest of the Trojans stayed to fight.

allQuestions.questionText: What happened when Hector finally met Achilles?
allQuestions.answerA: Hector defeated Achilles very easily.
allQuestions.answerB: They became friends, hugged, and stopped the war.
allQuestions.answerC: Achilles chased Hector around the walls and in the end killed him with his spear.

allQuestions.questionText: What cruel thing did Achilles do after he killed Hector?
allQuestions.answerA: He tied his dead body to his chariot and dragged it in the dirt back to the Achaean camp.
allQuestions.answerB: He immediately gave him a grand and honorable funeral.
allQuestions.answerC: He gave Hector's armor back to the Trojans.

allQuestions.questionText: What did the Achaeans do the next day in their camp?
allQuestions.answerA: They had a big feast and dances because Hector died.
allQuestions.answerB: They buried Patroclus with great honors and held funeral games (sports) in his memory.
allQuestions.answerC: They packed their things to leave secretly.

allQuestions.questionText: Why did the king of Troy, Priam, go secretly at night to Achilles' tent and what did he achieve?
allQuestions.answerA: He went to kill him in his sleep, but Achilles took him prisoner.
allQuestions.answerB: He went to ask for peace, and Achilles agreed that the Achaeans would leave.
allQuestions.answerC: He tearfully begged him to give him the body of his son (Hector) to bury it, and Achilles was moved and agreed.

allQuestions.questionText: What had his mother, the goddess Thetis, done to Achilles when he was a baby to make him immortal (invulnerable)?
allQuestions.answerA: She gave him the magic nectar of the Olympian gods to drink.
allQuestions.answerB: She dipped him into the river of the Underworld, but because she held him by the heel, that spot remained weak.
allQuestions.answerC: She put magic golden armor on him that nothing could pierce.

allQuestions.questionText: Which god advised Paris and how did he finally manage to kill the invincible Achilles?
allQuestions.answerA: The god Apollo, who helped him aim and shoot his arrow exactly in Achilles' heel.
allQuestions.answerB: The god Ares, who gave him a magic, fiery sword.
allQuestions.answerC: Zeus, who threw a thunderbolt to blind Achilles.

allQuestions.questionText: What happened immediately after the death of Achilles?
allQuestions.answerA: The Trojans took his body and hid it inside Troy.
allQuestions.answerB: A fierce battle took place, but Ajax and Odysseus fought bravely and saved his body.
allQuestions.answerC: The Achaeans got so scared that they got on their ships and left for Greece.

allQuestions.questionText: What finally happened to Paris, shortly after the death of Achilles?
allQuestions.answerA: He became the new king of Troy and made peace.
allQuestions.answerB: He secretly left with Helen of Troy and went to Egypt.
allQuestions.answerC: He was fatally wounded by the poisoned arrows of an Achaean (Philoctetes) and died.

allQuestions.questionText: What brilliant plan did the resourceful Odysseus come up with so the Achaeans could finally enter Troy?
allQuestions.answerA: To dig a huge underground tunnel beneath the walls.
allQuestions.answerB: To build a giant hollow wooden horse, the Trojan Horse.
allQuestions.answerC: To ask for peace and become friends with the Trojans.

allQuestions.questionText: What exactly was the Trojan Horse and what did it hide inside it?
allQuestions.answerA: It was a real, giant horse that ate people.
allQuestions.answerB: It was a magic statue that breathed fire from its mouth.
allQuestions.answerC: It was a wooden horse, and the bravest Achaean warriors hid in its belly.

allQuestions.questionText: How did the Achaeans manage to trick the Trojans into bringing the horse inside the city?
allQuestions.answerA: They pretended to leave with their ships and left the horse as a supposed gift for the goddess Athena.
allQuestions.answerB: They all dressed up as Trojan soldiers and passed through the gates.
allQuestions.answerC: They gave many gold coins to the guards to open the gates for them.

allQuestions.questionText: What did the seer Cassandra and the priest Laocoön tell the Trojans when they saw the Trojan Horse?
allQuestions.answerA: They told them to quickly bring it inside to have a big celebration.
allQuestions.answerB: They warned them not to bring it inside because it was a trap, but no one listened to them.
allQuestions.answerC: They told them to paint it gold so the gods would like it more.
